description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. 
 
 
 All roles require onsite presence a minimum of four days per week. Some roles may require five days onsite based on role responsibilities, business needs and manager discretion. Schedule flexibility may be available depending on the role and manager approval, including a 9/80 work schedule and compensatory time off (time off earned for hours worked beyond 40 per week) for eligible employees.


 Physical Sciences Laboratories (PSL) supports the effective and timely development and operation of national security systems through scientific research and the application of advanced technologies. PSL has more than 150 specialized laboratories used to test, analyze, and troubleshoot virtually every aspect of rocket and satellite system design, development, construction, deployment, and operation. The expertise of the laboratories' technical staff allows PSL to stay abreast of new technological developments and program support issues associated with rapidly evolving space systems.
  
 Our group designs, builds, and tests next-generation optical and hyperspectral imaging instruments supporting national security and civil space missions. We are hiring a Research Scientist or Senior Scientist to lead instrument integration & test, alignment, and calibration efforts for cutting-edge imaging spectrometer and optical sensing payloads. This role sits at the intersection of optical engineering, systems engineering, and flight hardware development, directly shaping the performance of instruments that fly on orbital, lunar, and planetary missions.

 Highlights of our lab's capabilities can be seen here: Virtual Tour 
  
 The selected candidate will be required to work full-time on-site at our facility in El Segundo, CA.

 What You'll Be Doing 
 Serve as technical lead for instrument integration & test (I&T), alignment, and calibration of optical/hyperspectral imaging instruments
 Design, build, and operate automated optical test benches and ground support equipment using Python/Matlab
 Lead or support payload-level and instrument-level performance modeling, error budgeting, and verification against requirements
 Act as Co-Investigator or instrument lead on new technology development and proposal efforts, partnering with PIs across the organization
 Provide technical direction and mentorship to junior engineers and students supporting I&T campaigns
 Interface directly with program customers, subcontractors, and cross-functional engineering teams to resolve design, integration, and test issues
 Apply Leadership Competency Model behaviors (Operates Strategically, Engages with Impact, Leads Change, Fosters Innovation, Deliver Results) to drive technical execution and team collaboration across multi-disciplinary programs
 
 What Corporate Skills You’ll Bring 
 Strong written and oral communication skills 
 Must work well in a team environment 
 Possess organizational, time management and project management skills 
 Demonstrate flexibility and ability to adapt to changing organizational need 
 Interpersonal skills to coordinate efforts and work with other internal and external organizations 
 
 What You Need to be Successful  
 Minimum Requirements for Research Scientist – Signal and Image Process Engineering and Physics:  
 Bachelor’s degree in Optics, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or related STEM field
 8 years of relevant research or engineering experience in optical systems, instrument I&T, or related hardware development
 Demonstrated hands-on experience with optical alignment, characterization, and calibration of instruments/testbeds
 Proficiency in Python and/or Matlab for test automation, data acquisition, and analysis
 Experience with optical design/ray-tracing tools (e.g., Zemax, Code V or OSLO, RayViz, or TracePro) and CAD tools (e.g., Solidworks)
 Willing to travel occasionally to customer sites/field campaigns, domestically, approx. 10–20%
 This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.
  
 In addition to the above, the minimum requirements for a Senior Scientist – Signal and Image Process Engineering and Physics:   
 12 years of relevant research or engineering experience in optical systems, instrument I&T, or related hardware development
 Experience leading optical sensor development projects through full lifecycle
 
 How You Can Stand Out 
 It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: 
 Demonstrated experience as an instrument I&T lead, payload lead, or Co-I on a flight or airborne imaging/sensing instrument
 Experience supporting NASA, DoD, or national security space missions from concept through delivery
 Track record of peer-reviewed publications or recognized research awards in optics, imaging systems, or photonics
 Experience managing or coordinating subcontractors and cross-functional technical teams
 Field campaign experience with airborne or in situ spectrometer/sensor measurements
 
 
 We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business.  The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below.  Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills. 
 
 (Min - Max)
$144,500.00 - $264,600.00 
 
Pay Basis: Annual 
 Leadership Competencies 
 Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who: 
 Operate Strategically 
 Lead Change    
 Engage with Impact    
 Foster Innovation    
 Deliver Results   
 
 Ways We Reward Our Employees 
 During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits.
 Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type.  A few highlights include: 
 Comprehensive health care and wellness plans

 Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation

 Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options

 401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire

 Flexible spending accounts

 Variable pay program for exceptional contributions

 Relocation assistance

 Professional growth and development programs to help advance your career

 Education assistance programs

 An inclusive work environment built on teamwork, flexibility, and respect

 
 We are all unique, from various backgrounds and all walks of life, yet one thing bonds all of us to each other—the belief that we can make a difference. This core belief empowers us to do our best work at The Aerospace Corporation.
 
 
 Equal Opportunity Commitment 
 The Aerospace Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, color, religion, genetic information, marital status, ancestry, national origin, protected veteran status, physical disability, medical condition, mental disability, or disability status and any other characteristic protected by state or federal law. If you’re an individual with a disability or a disabled veteran who needs assistance using our online job search and application tools or need reasonable accommodation to complete the job application process, please contact us by phone at 310.336.5432 or by email at  peoplemangmnt.mailbox@aero.org . You can also review  Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal .
